rule.recording_beside_entry: A dive without a recording and a dive with one are at the same time
rule.entry_apart_from_recording: Probably the same dive with another start time: the starts are {{difference}} apart, depth and duration agree

checks.how: If they are the same dive, merge them. If a time is wrong or one belongs to another Diver, open that dive and correct it there.
checks.keptApart: Kept as two dives. You are asked again if one of them changes its time.
checks.mergeAllBody: In each of these pairs one dive has a recording and the other has none, at the same time and about as deep: what an import puts together by itself. The dive with the recording is kept and takes over what it lacks from the other, which goes to “Deleted dives”.
checks.answeredIntro: Dives at the same time that you said are two dives.

short.title: Probably not dives
short.how: A recording shorter than {{duration}} that stayed above {{depth}} is usually a dive computer that got wet, or a false start. If it was no dive, delete it: it goes to “Deleted dives” and can be restored.
short.kept: Kept. You are asked again if its duration or depth changes.
short.answeredIntro: Short, shallow recordings that you said to keep.

merge.hint: Another dive in this logbook was at the same time: {{facts}}. If both are the same dive, you can merge them into one.
merge.title: Merge these two dives?
merge.hintKeepsOther: Merged, the other dive stays, because it has the recording.
merge.whyRecording: The dive with the recording stays.
merge.takes: The dive that stays takes over what it lacks from the other one: recordings, dive site, buddies and values. The other one’s notes are added to its own.
merge.linkMoves: It is then linked to the dive in {{name}}.
merge.other: You can restore the other one under “Deleted dives” on the logbook.
merge.pickIntro: These are the other dives in this logbook from the day before to the day after this one. Choose the one that is the same dive. You are asked again before anything is merged.
merge.pickNone: This logbook has no other dive from the day before to the day after this one. If the same dive is logged on another day, correct its date first.
merge.done: The two dives are one now.

divers.title: Divers
divers.intro: The Divers whose logbooks you keep. Your own comes first.
divers.notEmpty: Only Divers without dives or devices, who are on no dive, can be deleted.
divers.devicesIntro: Dive computers and transmitters that recorded your dives. Imports from a device go to the Diver it belongs to.

divers.sameName: You already have a Diver called {{name}}. That works, but the two will be hard to tell apart.

divers.noOthers: No other divers yet. Add them here, from a dive, or from your SSI buddy list on your account page.
divers.mergeIntro: Pick the diver who is {{name}}. The dives that list {{name}} then list that diver, and {{name}}’s accounts move to them. This can’t be undone.

sites.noMatchFilters: No dive sites match these filters.

siteImport.title: Import dive sites
siteImport.intro: Fetch dive sites from OpenStreetMap, Wikidata or SSI into this Dive Hub. Sites that are already here are updated where nobody changed them; what Users changed stays.
siteImport.adminLead: Fill the dive sites with data from OpenStreetMap, Wikidata and SSI, for a country, an area or everywhere.
siteImport.odblTitle: OpenStreetMap’s data comes with conditions (Open Database License).
siteImport.odblCredit: Wherever its data is shown, OpenStreetMap must be credited. Dive Hub does this on every site that has its data and on the list of dive sites.
siteImport.odblShareAlike: If you make the list of dive sites available to the public, you must offer it under the same license. A Dive Hub only invited people use, such as a family’s or club’s, doesn’t do that.
siteImport.odblConfirm: I understand and import OpenStreetMap data under these conditions
siteImport.ssiTitle: SSI gives no licence for its list of dive sites.
siteImport.ssiNoConditions: Unlike OpenStreetMap, there are no conditions you could accept that would make copying it allowed.
siteImport.ssiDatabase: In the EU the list is protected as a database, so copying large parts of it can infringe SSI’s rights.
siteImport.ssiRisk: Importing it is your decision as the operator of this Dive Hub, and your risk.
siteImport.ssiTaken: Taken per site: name, position, country, water type and SSI’s ID. Moderation comments, statistics and wildlife are never stored.
siteImport.ssiConfirm: I understand and import SSI’s dive sites at my own risk
siteImport.onlyFill: Only fill dive sites that are already here
siteImport.onlyFillHint: Creates no new sites. Matches the sources’ sites by ID, or by name and position, and fills them, e.g. with SSI IDs and water types.
siteImport.boxHint: Degrees; south and west are negative.
siteImport.worldHint: About 1,700 dive sites worldwide from OpenStreetMap and Wikidata, about 24,000 from SSI.
siteImport.languageHint: Where a source has names in several languages (Wikidata). OpenStreetMap’s local names are kept.
siteImport.needBox: Enter all four edges, with the south edge below the north edge.
siteImport.needOdbl: Confirm the conditions of OpenStreetMap’s data, or import from Wikidata only.
siteImport.needSsi: Confirm the explanation about SSI’s list, or leave SSI out.
siteImport.busy: An import is running. Start the next one when it’s done.

provider.importAsRecordingsHint: With their profile, like the computer’s own files.
provider.importAsEntriesHint: They only fill dives here, like dives typed in by hand.

aiAccess.offAdmin: AI access is switched off on this Dive Hub. You can switch it on under Admin.
aiAccess.offExisting: Your AI accesses don’t work until then.
aiAccess.sharedLead: Whatever the assistant reads is sent to the company behind it, such as Anthropic or OpenAI, and handled under that company’s terms, not this Dive Hub’s:
aiAccess.sharedDives: your dives with their profiles and notes, your divers and the dive sites
aiAccess.sharedBuddies: the names of the people you dived with, which is other people’s data
aiAccess.sharedPositions: where your dives started and ended, only if you allow it below
aiAccess.sharedLog: Below you see what was read. You can revoke an access at any time.

aiAccess.setupLead: To connect, use the line for your assistant. Each one already contains the key:

aiAccess.setupMcpRemote: Other assistants: the command for mcp-remote

aiAccess.empty: You have no AI access yet.

aiAccess.adminLead: Users can let an AI assistant read their own logbook through this Dive Hub (its MCP endpoint, read-only). What an assistant reads is sent to its provider, under that provider’s terms. While this is off, no key works and none can be created.
aiAccess.adminOffBody: Every key stops working at once. The accesses stay and work again when you switch it back on.

aiAccess.adminRevokeAllBody_other: The keys of all {{count}} AI accesses stop working and can’t be brought back. Users have to create new ones.

With symptoms after a dive (unusual tiredness, joint pain, skin changes, numbness, dizziness), call DAN or the emergency services.

guidance.ascent_rate: Tables and dive computers assume about 9 to 10 m/min (30 ft/min). In experiments faster ascents gave more bubbles, and 10 m/min with a stop the fewest.
guidance.last_metres: Pressure changes fastest near the surface, so the last metres matter most. BSAC asks for a minute for the last 6 m (20 ft); many divers are faster after a stop, so Dive Hub remarks on them only above 18 m/min (60 ft/min), twice what the rest of the ascent is held to.
guidance.safety_stop: A stop of 3 minutes at 3 to 6 m cut bubbles by about a factor of ten after dives without decompression stops. 5 minutes are advised after dives deeper than 30 m (100 ft) or close to the no-decompression limit; longer showed no further gain.
guidance.descent_rate: No study links descent speed to harm. Ear and sinus squeeze are the most common diving injuries, and DAN advises equalising early and often.
guidance.stop_stability: Training standards (GUE Fundamentals) ask to hold a stop within 1.5 m (5 ft). Small movements have no shown effect on decompression: this is feedback on buoyancy control.
guidance.ndl: Risk rises toward the no-decompression limit (DAN 2025). The limit is not a line between safe and unsafe.
guidance.ceiling: Decompression stops are obligations of the plan your computer follows. Garmin tolerates 0.6 m (2 ft) above a ceiling before it alerts.
guidance.ppo2: NOAA’s limits use 1.4 bar as the working limit and 1.6 bar for contingencies. The risk of oxygen toxicity rises with pressure and time.
guidance.cns: The CNS percentage counts oxygen exposure against NOAA’s limits: 80 % is the usual planning limit, 100 % the limit itself.
guidance.sawtooth: Agencies advise against sawtooth profiles, based on reports of instructors with many ascents. Slow up-and-down schedules with a stop gave almost no bubbles in a field study. No threshold is backed by evidence; this one is cautious on purpose (4 times 6 m).
guidance.reverse_profile: A 1999 workshop of the Smithsonian and DAN found no reason to forbid a deeper dive after a shallower one for dives without decompression stops, shallower than 40 m and less than 12 m apart. Outside that there is little data either way.
guidance.surface_interval: Longer surface intervals lower the odds of decompression sickness (about 6 % per hour in DAN Europe’s data). An hour before a dive deeper than 18 m (60 ft) is a convention, not a tested minimum.
guidance.dives_per_day: BSAC advises at most 3 dives a day. It is an agency rule: liveaboard diving with more had the lowest rate of decompression sickness in DAN’s Project Dive Exploration.
guidance.deep_days: BSAC advises a break after 4 days of dives deeper than 30 m (100 ft). It is an agency rule: measured bubbles fell over consecutive diving days.

recommendation.ascent_rate: Start the ascent early enough to take it slowly, and watch your computer’s ascent indicator, most of all in the shallower half.
recommendation.last_metres: After the stop, let the last metres take their time.
recommendation.safety_stop: Plan gas and time for the stop, and hold it for the full time when conditions allow.
recommendation.descent_rate: If equalising was easy, nothing to change. If not, descend more slowly through the first metres.
recommendation.stop_stability: A visual reference (a line, the reef) and slow breathing make a stop easier to hold.
recommendation.ndl: Leave more margin where you can: start up earlier, and extend the safety stop to 5 minutes.
recommendation.ceiling: Hold stops at or just below the depth your computer shows. After a missed stop, follow your computer’s and your agency’s procedure, and watch for symptoms.
recommendation.ppo2: Check the maximum operating depth of your gas before the dive and stay above it.
recommendation.cns: Plan repetitive nitrox dives with the oxygen clock in mind: a leaner mix, shallower, or a longer surface interval.
recommendation.sawtooth: Where the site allows, follow its contour instead of going up and down, and keep ascents slow.
recommendation.reverse_profile: Nothing to change by itself. Outside those bounds, plan the second dive with extra margin.
recommendation.surface_interval: Where the day allows, take the longer break before the deeper dive.
recommendation.dives_per_day: On days with many dives, keep the later ones shallower and the stops long.
recommendation.deep_days: Consider a shallower day or a day off in a long series of deep dives.
